title: Ctrl+Alt+Timeline
blurb: Your feed, your playlist, your paycheck, and the decades they secretly overlap.

cards.say: [Netflix mailed out its very last rental DVD in 2023], [Netflix mailed out VHS tapes until it switched to DVDs in 1999], [Blockbuster passed on buying Netflix for 50 million dollars in 2000], and [Netflix was founded in 1997 but didn't start streaming until 2007].
cards.real: Netflix never rented VHS. Tapes were too bulky to mail cheaply, so the founders bet on brand-new DVDs from the start.

cards.say: [IKEA sold pens and wallets for five years before it sold furniture], [Slack began as a side tool at a company making an online game], [Twitch grew out of a site where one man livestreamed his life around the clock], and [Shopify grew out of an online store its founders ran to sell surfboards].
cards.real: Shopify grew out of Snowdevil, an online store selling snowboards. Its founders built their own shop software for it in 2004, then turned that into Shopify.

cards.say: [Kendrick Lamar won a 2018 Pulitzer Prize for his album To Pimp a Butterfly], [All I Want for Christmas Is You first hit number one 25 years after release], [Kate Bush topped the UK chart in 2022 with a song from 1985], and [Never Gonna Give You Up passed one billion YouTube views in 2021].
cards.real: Kendrick Lamar's 2018 Pulitzer Prize for Music was for DAMN. He was the first winner from outside classical music and jazz.
src: NOT WEB-CHECKED (textbook: Running Up That Hill hit UK number one in June 2022) https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Running_Up_That_Hill

cards.say: [Tom Brady was the 199th pick in the 2000 NFL draft], [the St. Louis Blues were last in the NHL in January 2019 and won the Stanley Cup that June], [Lionel Messi's first Barcelona deal was written on a pizza box in 2000], and [the 2016 Warriors won 73 games and still lost the NBA Finals].
cards.real: Messi's first agreement with Barcelona, in December 2000, was famously scribbled on a paper napkin.
src: NOT WEB-CHECKED (textbook: Brady was pick 199 in the 2000 draft) https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Brady
NOT WEB-CHECKED (textbook: the December 2000 napkin agreement) https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lionel_Messi

cards.say: [The viral Trololo video was actually filmed for Soviet TV in 1976], [the animal in the Dramatic Chipmunk video is a prairie dog], [the Charlie Bit My Finger video sold as an NFT for over 750,000 dollars], and [Vine launched in 2013 with a ten-second limit on every video].
cards.real: Vine clips could be at most six seconds long. The app launched in January 2013, and that tiny limit is what made its looping videos famous.
src: NOT WEB-CHECKED (textbook: Vine launched in January 2013 with a six-second limit on clips) https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vine_(service)

cards.say: [Microsoft bought Minecraft for 250 million dollars in 2014], [Apple's third co-founder sold his 10 percent share for 800 dollars], [Twitter's first bird logo was stock art bought for under 20 dollars], and [Instagram had 13 employees when Facebook bought it for a billion dollars].
cards.real: Microsoft paid 2.5 billion dollars for Mojang, the studio behind Minecraft, in 2014.

cards.say: [Android was first built to run digital cameras], [Angry Birds was the 52nd game its studio made], [the first iPhone had a front camera for selfies], and [epidemiologists studied a 2005 plague in World of Warcraft].
cards.real: The original 2007 iPhone had only a rear camera. Front cameras arrived with the iPhone 4 in 2010.

cards.say: [New VCRs were still being manufactured in 2016], [the world's last Blockbuster store closed its doors in 2019], [Japan's last pager service didn't shut down until 2019], and [AOL still offered dial-up internet in 2025].
cards.real: The Blockbuster in Bend, Oregon, became the last one on Earth in 2019, and it was still renting movies in 2024.

cards.say: [Netflix's Roma was the first streaming film to win Best Picture], [Return of the King won every one of the 11 Oscars it was up for], [in 2025 a Chinese film became the highest-grossing animated movie ever], and [Mickey Mouse's first version entered the public domain in 2024].
cards.real: Roma lost Best Picture in 2019 to Green Book. The first streaming film to win was Apple's CODA, in 2022.

cards.say: [The word robot comes from a Czech play written in 1920], [Oxford's Word of the Year for 2015 was an emoji, not a word], [selfie was named Oxford's Word of the Year in 2013], and [the Python language, released in 1991, was named after the snake].
cards.real: Guido van Rossum named Python after the British comedy show Monty Python's Flying Circus, not the snake.

cards.say: [In 2021 Reddit users sent GameStop's stock up over 1,000 percent], [Jack Dorsey's first tweet sold as an NFT for 29 million dollars], [Nvidia became the first company worth 4 trillion dollars in 2025], and [in 2017 a game about cartoon cats clogged up the Ethereum network].
cards.real: Jack Dorsey's first tweet sold as an NFT in March 2021 for about 2.9 million dollars, a tenth of that.
src: NOT WEB-CHECKED (textbook: GameStop went from under 20 dollars to over 300 dollars in January 2021 in the WallStreetBets short squeeze) https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GameStop_short_squeeze

cards.say: [Microsoft was founded in Albuquerque, New Mexico, in 1975], [McDonald's was once the biggest investor in Chipotle], [Starbucks is named after the ship's captain in Moby-Dick], and [Airbnb began with three air mattresses on an apartment floor].
cards.real: Starbuck is the first mate of the whaling ship in Moby-Dick. The captain is Ahab.
